description: We are a team of high school students with strong backgrounds in software development and data science, including web development and AI. We are looking for team members with strong skills in areas that complement our technical background, especially agriculture, engineering, science, and research. Our goal is to build a competitive project and reach NASA Global.
summary:
AGRI-GO is an AI-powered smart agriculture platform designed to help Egyptian farmers make data-driven decisions and improve agricultural sustainability. By integrating NASA POWER, FAO WaPOR, Copernicus Sentinel-2, ERA5, and FAO GAEZ datasets, AGRI-GO analyzes farm-specific environmental and agricultural conditions.

Farmers can select one of three strategies: preserving soil health, maximizing crop production, or saving water. Based on the selected goal, the platform evaluates suitable crops and ranks the top five recommendations using available scientific data.

AGRI-GO also transforms real farm boundaries into an interactive 3D virtual farm, allowing farmers to visualize crop layouts, growth stages, and irrigation systems. Furthermore, it enables farmers to simulate different environmental conditions on their own land, such as changes in temperature, water availability, and other climate factors, and explore their potential effects on crop growth and productivity.

The platform connects environmental monitoring, crop management, water-use analysis, and economic assessments to help farmers understand potential costs, production, and profitability.

By combining Earth observation data, agricultural intelligence, environmental simulation, and 3D visualization in a simple, farmer-friendly interface, AGRI-GO aims to support more informed decisions, efficient resource use, and sustainable agriculture in Egypt.
details:
AGRI-GO – Smart Agriculture Platform

AGRI-GO is a smart agriculture platform designed to help farmers make better decisions about their farmland using agricultural, environmental, and geographical data.

The idea came from the challenges farmers face when deciding what to grow, how to manage water resources, and how to make their farms more productive without increasing costs or putting additional pressure on the soil.

The platform starts by allowing farmers to select their farmland on an interactive Google Map and draw its exact boundaries. This provides a starting point for analyzing their land and making agricultural recommendations based on its geographical and environmental conditions.

Farmers can choose between three agricultural strategies depending on their priorities:

  • Soil Health: Focusing on maintaining soil quality and supporting long-term sustainability.
  • Maximum Production: Focusing on choosing crops and growing conditions that can improve productivity.
  • Water Saving: Focusing on reducing unnecessary water consumption and improving irrigation efficiency.

Based on the selected strategy and available agricultural information, the platform recommends the five most suitable crops from its crop library.

AGRI-GO also includes an interactive 3D virtual farm where farmers can visualize their land, arrange crops, experiment with planting layouts, and explore irrigation systems. Other sections provide crop information, environmental monitoring, agricultural planning, and economic analysis, including estimated cultivation costs, expected production, revenues, and potential profits.

We wanted to bring these different aspects together because choosing a crop is not just an agricultural decision. Farmers also need to consider available resources, environmental conditions, and whether the final result makes economic sense.

Benefits and Expected Impact

AGRI-GO aims to make agricultural information easier to understand and use. Instead of relying on different sources for crop information, weather conditions, water management, and financial calculations, farmers can access these tools through one platform.

It can help farmers make more informed crop choices, manage water resources more efficiently, plan their farms, and better understand the potential financial outcomes of their decisions.

Our goal is to support more sustainable and productive agriculture by helping farmers make better use of available resources. While we initially considered challenges that are particularly relevant to Egypt, such as water scarcity and changing environmental conditions, these challenges are shared by agricultural communities in many parts of the world.

In the long term, we hope AGRI-GO can be adapted to different geographical regions and agricultural conditions, making data-driven farming more accessible to farmers wherever they operate.

Technologies and Data Sources

We built AGRI-GO as a web-based application using:

  • React for building the user interface.
  • TypeScript for application development.
  • HTML and CSS for the structure and design.
  • Google Maps API for interactive maps and selecting farmland boundaries.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber for building the interactive 3D farm environment.

For agricultural and environmental analysis, we identified scientific data sources including NASA POWER, FAO WaPOR, Copernicus Sentinel-2, FAO GAEZ, and ERA5.

These sources provide different types of information, including weather conditions, water productivity, satellite imagery, vegetation data, and crop suitability information.

What Makes AGRI-GO Different

One of the main features we wanted to introduce was the 3D virtual farm.

Most agricultural platforms present information through charts, maps, or text. We wanted to give farmers a different way to interact with their land. Through the 3D environment, they can visualize their farms, arrange crops, and explore different planting layouts instead of just reading recommendations.

We also wanted the platform to go beyond simply recommending crops. The three agricultural strategies allow farmers to approach the same farmland from different perspectives. A farmer whose priority is saving water may make a different choice from someone focused on maximizing production.

Combining these recommendations with farm visualization, environmental information, and economic analysis makes AGRI-GO a more complete tool for agricultural planning.

Factors We Considered During Development

Throughout development, we focused on the factors that influence agricultural decisions, including water availability, soil health, climate conditions, crop suitability, and economic feasibility.

We also considered the importance of using reliable scientific data while recognizing that agricultural recommendations depend on several factors and that environmental models have limitations.

Another important consideration was usability. Agricultural technology should not become more complicated than the problems it is supposed to solve. That is why we focused on creating a straightforward, Arabic-friendly interface that makes the platform's tools accessible without requiring technical knowledge.
